2. Since f is a step function, it can be written as a finite linear combination of indicator functions of the subintervals [x_i, x_{i+1}]. Let c_i be the constant value of f on the subinterval [x_i, x_{i+1}].

5. Since f is bounded, there exists a constant M such that |f(x)| \leq M for all x in [a, b].
6. Using the definition of the Riemann integral, we can show that the Riemann integral of f is equal to the sum of the areas of the rectangles formed by the step function, which is bounded by M(b-a).

Therefore, we have shown that a step function f / [a, b] -> \mathbb{R} is Riemann Integrable if and only if it is bounded and has at most a countable number of discontinuities.
